title: Mastering Price Elasticity and Anchoring
description: Learn to use elasticity analysis, willingness-to-pay research, A/B pricing tests, and anchoring to optimize prices.

interactions.prompt: If a 10% price increase causes a 20% drop in units sold, what is the price elasticity of demand?

options.text: -2.0 (elastic)
-0.5 (inelastic)
-1.0 (unit elastic)
2.0 (perfectly elastic)

interactions.teachingPreamble: Price elasticity of demand measures how sensitive customer purchasing is to price changes. It's calculated as % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price. When Netflix raised its U.S. streaming price from $9.99 to $10.99 in 2017, subscriber growth barely slowed — a sign of inelastic demand.

interactions.prompt: A SaaS company tests three price points: $29/mo (1,200 signups), $39/mo (1,050 signups), $49/mo (620 signups). Total revenue is $34,800, $40,950, and $30,380 respectively. What's the key insight?

options.text: Demand is perfectly linear across all three prices
$39 maximizes revenue; demand drops sharply above it
$29 is optimal because it drives the most customers
All three prices generate roughly equal profit

interactions.prompt: Which method best captures willingness-to-pay without directly asking customers to name a price?

options.text: Open-ended survey: 'What would you pay?'
Van Westendorp price sensitivity meter with four threshold questions
Conjoint analysis using feature tradeoff scenarios
Competitor price benchmarking from public websites

interactions.teachingPreamble: Willingness-to-pay (WTP) research uncovers how much customers will actually spend. Direct questions ('What would you pay?') are notoriously unreliable — people understate to get lower prices. Companies like Porsche and HubSpot use conjoint analysis, which presents tradeoff scenarios between features and prices, forcing respondents to reveal true preferences indirectly.

interactions.prompt: In A/B pricing tests, showing different prices to different users at the same time risks ____ backlash if customers discover the discrepancy, as Amazon learned in 2000.

options.text: Price discrimination
Regulatory compliance
Inventory shortage
Brand dilution

interactions.prompt: You're launching a project management tool. Conjoint analysis shows WTP of $15/user/mo, but your closest competitor Asana charges $10.99. Do you:

options.text: Price at $10.49 to undercut and win market share
Price at $14.99 anchored to your WTP data with premium positioning
Launch free forever and monetize with ads
Match Asana at $10.99 and compete on features alone

interactions.prompt: A luxury hotel lists a $1,200/night penthouse suite at the top of its booking page. How does this primarily affect the perception of a $350/night standard room?

options.text: It makes the $350 room feel like a bargain by comparison
It confuses customers and increases bounce rates
It signals the hotel is overpriced across all tiers
It has no effect since customers only compare competitors

interactions.teachingPreamble: Anchoring is a cognitive bias where the first number people see heavily influences their judgment of subsequent numbers. The Economist famously offered a print-only subscription at $125, a web-only at $59, and print+web at $125 — the 'useless' middle option anchored buyers toward the combo deal, boosting revenue by 43% in Dan Ariely's study.

interactions.prompt: You're optimizing pricing for a B2B analytics platform with no prior pricing data. Rank these steps from first to last in a sound price optimization process.

options.text: Run A/B tests on the top two candidate price points
Conduct conjoint analysis to measure customer WTP
Analyze elasticity from live sales data after launch
Design tiered packages with anchoring-optimized positioning

interactions.prompt: Your WTP research pointed to $39/mo and A/B tests confirmed it. But a new competitor just launched a free tier with 80% of your features. How should you respond?

options.text: Drop to $19/mo immediately to stay competitive on price
Keep $39/mo, add a limited free tier, and anchor upgrades aggressively
Match them with a fully free product and pivot to enterprise sales
Ignore the competitor since your WTP data is already validated

interactions.priorContext: Previously you validated $39/mo through conjoint analysis and A/B testing with strong conversion. Now a well-funded competitor has launched a free tier covering most of your core features, shifting the competitive landscape and potentially resetting customer price expectations.
